A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same TT-VLA work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices S1-S13 support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original TT-VLA simulation and real-robot experiments, ablations, comparison results, and qualitative rollouts in Tables 1-3, Figures 3-5, and Figure S1.

after.justification: v3 retains these original simulation, real-robot, ablation, and qualitative results, including the appendix rollouts.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same VLAC progress estimator, progress-difference reward, value-free PPO objective, and online policy-update procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate 15 simulation tasks and nine real-world tasks across execution, vision, and semantics. Dist Recep. and M Recep. remain distinct retained scenarios with unchanged definitions in Appendix S3; exchanging their table labels does not change coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Nora, OpenVLA, OpenVLA-RL, and TraceVLA. The GAE comparison in Figure 4 and TLM/TTRL comparisons in Table 3 also retain the same comparator membership.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1 and S3-S5 retain the same trial counts, image resolutions, warm-up budgets, LoRA settings, 160-step episode horizon, and update-interval evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: The reward/advantage and update-frequency ablations, distribution-shift evaluations, and real-world case studies are unchanged, including the additional rollouts in Appendix S6 and Figure S1.

E5.justification: Both versions report three random seeds for simulation. Repeated-run information and uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 1 exchanges the Dist Recep. and M Recep. headers without changing numerical cells. The OpenVLA/OpenVLA+TT-VLA pair 20.42%/29.58% moves from Dist Recep. to M Recep., while 43.75%/45.00% moves oppositely. Section 4.2 correspondingly reassigns the 44.9% relative gain to M Recep. The unchanged Figure 2(b) retains the earlier score-to-task association, creating a discrepancy. Other results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, objectives, Proposition 1, Corollary 1, Lemma 1, and proofs, including Appendix S2, are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, conclusion, and Appendix S9 retain the same contributions and claims about progress-guided test-time adaptation and improved generalization across SFT- and RL-based VLAs.

C2.justification: v3 deletes the main Limitations section, removing explicit warnings about ambiguous or occluded observations, non-monotonic task progress, and weak or poorly aligned base policies. These specific qualifications are not retained elsewhere; Appendix S11 preserves more general reward-reliability and safety cautions. Other result interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, RTX 6000 Ada hardware, demonstration-data information, pseudocode, and the promised code release upon acceptance are unchanged. Availability and licensing disclosures remain in Appendix S10 despite removal of the main ethics paragraph.

R1.justification: The reference list and related-work positioning are unchanged, including the EVOLVE-VLA discussion and Appendix S1. Bibliography differences arise from text reflow.

P1.justification: v3 removes the standalone Limitations and Ethical Considerations sections, adds a funding disclosure, marks Dongfang Liu as an additional corresponding author, and revises one task name in the results discussion. The remaining narrative and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 exchanges two semantic-task column headers. Removing the main-text sections reflows the references, while the figures, numerical table bodies, and appendix layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Table 1's revised task attribution conflicts with unchanged Figure 2(b): the radar plots still show higher M Recep. than Dist Recep. success, opposite to the revised table for Nora and OpenVLA. v3 also removes specific failure-condition caveats without restoring them in the appendices. These localized changes reduce reporting consistency and transparency about applicability; the retained appendix ethics and reproducibility disclosures limit the broader loss.
